decisive_items: history of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks prior to the development of the current eruption at the same site
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the upper dermis admixed with eosinophils and plasma cells
response.rationale: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma is favored by the eruption at a prior HSV-2 site, a mixed infiltrate with eosinophils/plasma cells, and absent clonal TCR rearrangement on repeat testing; the weak clonal band is not sustained and epidermotropism can occur in reactive pseudolymphomas, making CTCL/Mycosis fungoides less likely.

rejected.why: Same entity but less specific; lacks the cutaneous qualifier and does not incorporate the polyclonal/rearrangement-negative molecular evidence.
Mycosis fungoides is unlikely because repeat TCR studies showed no clonal rearrangement and the infiltrate was mixed with eosinophils/plasma cells.
Lymphomatoid papulosis is not supported; lesions are persistent plaques/nodules rather than self-resolving papules and CD30 is not described.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is contradicted by the absence of a persistent clonal TCR rearrangement and the reactive mixed infiltrate.
Dermatitis is too nonspecific and contradicted by smooth firm plaques/nodules and atypical lymphoid infiltrate.
